We seek candidates who can affirm and contribute to our mission. Providence College is also an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering a Beloved Community— an environment that reflects the rich diversity of the human family and is marked by justice, charity and the promotion of the common good and flourishing of all. We invite applications from qualified individuals who possess the experience, knowledge and commitment to develop the diverse learning environment envisioned as part of the Beloved Community. Women and minority candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. The College’s Non-Discrimination policy can be found Notice of Non-Discrimination (PDF document) (Download PDF reader) Overview The Department of Nursing at Providence College (also referred to as “the College” or “PC”) invites applications for a full-time Assistant Clinical Professor of Nursing to join our growing and mission-driven program beginning August 2027. We are seeking an innovative and student-centered educator with expertise in Medical Surgical Nursing who is excited to shape the future of nursing education at PC. The ideal candidate will be able to make meaningful connections between best practices in nursing education, a commitment to the dignity of the whole person, and the Catholic mission and identity of the College. The successful faculty member will play a pivotal role in designing and delivering high-impact clinical experiences that prepare undergraduate nursing students to lead with excellence, compassion, and integrity. They will collaborate closely with an enthusiastic team of faculty and professional staff to advance our cutting-edge teaching and simulation facilities and contribute to a dynamic curriculum that integrates leadership development, evidence-based practice, and holistic patient care. The new faculty member will teach Medical Surgical Nursing I and Medical Surgical Nursing II Clinicals. Clinical Nursing faculty at PC contribute to college and professional service in accordance with expectations for clinical faculty which include teaching excellence and service to the college. If desired, scholarship can also be a component of the role and mentoring in this area is provided through the Department of Nursing. Candidates with an earned master’s and professional clinical training in the medical surgicalnursing specialty are strongly encouraged to apply.The Assistant Clinical Professor of Nursing will report to the Department Chair and provide high-quality undergraduate clinical instruction. Primary responsibilities include developing, delivering, and assessing clinical courses and experiential learning activities that reflect evidence-based practice and support the mission of Providence College. The medical-surgical faculty member will collaborate closely with simulation, lab, and didactic faculty to ensure alignment between didactic content, skills acquisition, simulation based learning, and clinical application. Because nursing skills, clinical judgment, and patient care concepts are integrated throughout the medical surgical nursing sequence, this faculty member will play an important role in supporting curricular continuity across classroom, lab, simulation, and clinicallearning environments. Additional duties include advising undergraduate nursing students, contributing to curriculum development, and participating in departmental and college services such as committee work, program review, and accreditation activities. The faculty member is expected to support students’ professional growth by fostering leadership skills, clinical judgment, and research literacy within a collaborative, student-centered environment.A doctoral degree is required for this faculty appointment.This is an exciting and historic opportunity to join PC’s newly established School of Nursing and Health Sciences as it shapes an innovative, interdisciplinary curriculum for the next generation of students entering nursing and other health professions. The 153,000 sq. ft state-of-the-art Ben Mondor Center for Nursing and Health Sciences houses the School of Nursing and Health Sciences’ existing and future undergraduate and graduate programs. This one-of-a-kind facility opened in January 2025 and features the latest classroom design and technologies and showcases expansive clinical simulation and researchfacilities. A student career education and advising center, along with conference and meeting space, is included as part of the inspiring resources intended for the next generation of healthcare providers, faculty, and staff. Position Information Position Information Posting Number F00394 Position Title Assistant Professor, MSW Program (1-Year Limited) Division Academic Affairs Division Department Name School of Social Work Position Type Faculty Position Overview The position is responsible for teaching in the MSW Program, with a focus on social work practice, generalist practice, policy, and seminar courses. The faculty member will support student success through academic advisement, field internship liaison responsibilities, and facilitation of field seminars. The position also includes engagement in scholarly research, professional development, community service, and curriculum development. The faculty member will contribute to departmental and college activities and collaborate with colleagues to advance the mission of the MSW Program. Overall, the position supports the preparation of skilled, ethical, and socially responsive social work professionals through teaching, mentorship, scholarship, and service. Essential Duties Teach in the MSW Program, particularly in the following areas: Practice, Generalist practice, Policy, Seminar courses. Act as liaison to students in field internships, and facilitate field seminars. Provide academic advisement to students . Engage in scholarly research and professional activities. Participate in curriculum development for the MSW program. Engage in professional community service. Participate in other departmental and college activities as required. Occasional Duties Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Dean, School of Social Work or Chair of the MSW program. Required Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities Excellent oral and written communication skills. Ability to participate as a member of a team with faculty and staff. Ability to teach with cultural humility and curiosity in a collegial environment dedicated to student learning and engagement Experience in the development and delivery of hybrid, and online instruction at the undergraduate or graduate levels. Demonstrated knowledge and expertise in practice with diverse populations and commitment to anti-racism and social justice. Expertise in at least one substantive area (e.g. child welfare, homelessness, substance use). Ability to use data and research that support best practices in historical marginalized communities. Required Qualifications MSW degree from CSWE-accredited institution. At least two years post-MSW social work clinical practice experience in working with historically marginalized communities. Preferred Qualifications Teaching experience in social work at the graduate level. Experience in working with LatinX and Black communities and issues affecting the LatinX and/or Black population. Bilingual (English/Spanish). Environmental Conditions Teaching/instruction is performed in a traditional classroom setting and /or computer lab with chalkboards and adequate ventilation and lighting. Position Details FLSA Exempt Full Time / Part Time Full-time Proposed Compensation Additional compensation may be added for teaching at the collegiate level or other relevant experience. The successful candidate will hold a faculty appointment with primary teaching responsibilities in Health Sciences, while collaborating with faculty in Nursing and related majors focused on preparing students for careers in the health professions. As a tenured faculty member, the successful candidate will maintain an active program of scholarship consistent with their discipline, as well as mentor health sciences faculty to develop their scholarly goals and accomplishments.
